Chapter 7: Navigating Setbacks and Finding New Joys.
Let’s be honest—no journey ever follows a straight line. Even when your spirit is strong, setbacks are just part of the deal. As time went on, the challenges of Parkinson’s started to stand out more and more. There were days when your body just wouldn’t cooperate, and it felt like frustration might completely drown out any hope you had left.
And then there was advocacy work. That brought its own kind of letdowns. Maybe a promising research project stalled out. Or you hit another wall of red tape. Sometimes it seemed like everything moved at a snail’s pace.
But here’s the beautiful twist—in the middle of all those struggles, unexpected joys started to appear. Life slowed down, and with that slower pace came a real, deeper appreciation for those little moments you might’ve missed before. There was time to notice sunlight streaming through the window, or to truly enjoy a meal with family. Even a joke—one you might’ve let slip by—could spark genuine laughter. Suddenly, the world wasn’t just a blur of deadlines and demands. It was full of details, richer than ever.
Creativity found fresh ways to bloom. Acting, which once felt like the center of everything, became just one thread in a bigger, more colorful tapestry. There was writing, music, and the simple joy of telling stories to anyone willing to listen. That old urge to prove yourself faded away. What took its place? A desire to share, to connect, and to leave something meaningful behind.
Of course, setbacks didn’t disappear. There were still moments when old fears crept in, and the future felt shaky. But each time, leaning on loved ones, soaking up encouragement from friends, and drawing on that resilience you’ve built up over the years—it all made it possible to keep moving forward.
You start to realize something important: joy isn’t about living without pain. It’s about finding the light, even when things seem darkest.
Most people don’t realize just how much strength shows up in those small victories. Getting out of bed when it’s tough, making someone else smile, finishing a project that once looked impossible—these become your new measures of success.
This journey? It’s not about clearing every hurdle. It’s about learning to live fully, even when the road gets rough.
